'''Albert J.R. Heck''' (born 25 November 1964) is a Dutch scientist and professor at [[Utrecht University]], the [[Netherlands]] in the field of [[mass spectrometry]] and [[proteomics]]. He is known for his work on technologies to study proteins in their natural environment, with the aim to understand their biological function. Albert Heck was awarded the [[Spinoza Prize]] in 2017, the highest scientific award in the Netherlands.

== Biography ==
Albert Heck was born in [[Goes]], Netherlands. He studied [[chemistry]] at the [[Vrije Universiteit|VU University]] in Amsterdam, and received his PhD degree from the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1993. After a [[postdoctoral fellowship|postdoctoral period]] at [[Stanford University]] in the lab of [[Richard Zare]] and [[Sandia National Laboratories]] (Livermore) he became a postdoctoral fellow and later lecturer at [[University of Warwick]].

In 1998 he accepted a chair at [[Utrecht University]] as head of the Biomolecular Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics Group.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://profs.library.uu.nl/index.php/profrec/getprofdata/820/1/3/0|title=Catalogus Professorum: Prof.dr. A.J.R. Heck|publisher=UU|access-date=29 November 2019}}</ref> His group is part of the Departments of Chemistry and Pharmaceutical Sciences of the Faculty of Science.<ref>{{cite news
| title = Hoogleraren
| url = http://www.volkskrant.nl/vk/nl/2844/Archief/archief/article/detail/3311179/2012/09/05/Hoogleraren.dhtml
| access-date = 21 May 2014
| publisher = [[Volkskrant]]
| date = 5 September 2012
| language = Dutch }}</ref> From 2006 until 2012 Heck was scientific director of the [[Bijvoet Centre for Biomolecular Research]], and from 2015 to 2018 scientific director of the Utrecht Institute for Pharmaceutical Science at [[Utrecht University]]. In 2017 he received a Distinguished Faculty professorship of Utrecht University.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uu.nl/en/news/albert-heck-appointed-distinguished-professor-of-the-faculty-of-science|title=Albert Heck appointed Distinguished Professor of the Faculty of Science|date=1 November 2017|access-date=7 January 2020}}</ref>

== Research ==
The research of Albert Heck is focused on the development and use of mass spectrometry to study all cellular proteins. Within his research group, there are three main lines of research, improvement of instrumentation and analytical methods, proteomics and mass spectrometry based [[structural biology]], including [[native state|native]] protein mass spectrometry and [[cross-link]]ing mass spectrometry.

Albert Heck is regarded as one of the pioneers of native mass spectrometry.<ref>{{cite web
| title = Awards – 2013 Recipients
| url = http://www.hupo.org/about-hupo/awards/
| access-date = 21 May 2014
| publisher = HUPO }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Leney|first1=Aneika C.|last2=Heck|first2=Albert J. Albert Heck is closely involved in coordinating access to proteomics infrastructures in the Netherlands and in Europe. Since 2003 Heck is scientific director of the [[Netherlands Proteomics Centre]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theanalyticalscientist.com/fields-applications/proteins-at-work|publisher=The Analytical Scientist|title= Proteins At Work|date=23 February 2014}}</ref> From 2011 to 2015 he was coordinator of PRIME-XS,<ref>{{cite journal
| title = PRIME-XS, a European infrastructure for proteomics.
| journal = Molecular & Cellular Proteomics
| volume = 13
| issue = 8
| pages = 1901–1904
| doi = 10.1074/mcp.E114.040162
| pmid = 24958170
| pmc = 4125724
| year = 2014
| last1 = Raijmakers
| first1 = Reinout
| last2 = Olsen
| first2 = Jesper V.
| last3 = Aebersold
| first3 = Ruedi
| last4 = Heck
| first4 = Albert J. R.
| doi-access = free
}}</ref> and since 2019 he coordinates EPIC-XS,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.technologynetworks.com/proteomics/blog/proteomics-experts-unite-for-epic-xs-317152|publisher=Technology Networks|date=22 March 2019|access-date=29 November 2019|title=Proteomics Experts Unite for EPIC-XS}}</ref> both collaborative projects funded by the [[European Union]] to enable access to [[proteomics]] technology for researchers throughout Europe.

== Honours and awards ==
Heck received numerous awards and prizes for his scientific contributions. He received The [[KNCV]] golden medal in 2001,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kncv.nl/prijzen/kncv-gouden-medaille/winnaars-kncv-gouden-medaille|title=Overzicht KNCV Gouden Medaille Winnaars|language=NL|publisher=[[KNCV]]|access-date=29 November 2019}}</ref> the [[Descartes-Huygens Prize]] from the [[Académie de Sciences]] in 2006,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/awards/laureates/descartes-huygens-prize|title=Descartes-Huygens Prize|publisher=[[KNAW]]|access-date=29 November 2019|archive-date=22 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322164033/https://www.knaw.nl/en/awards/laureates/descartes-huygens-prize}}</ref> the Life Science Award of the German Mass Spectrometry Society in 2010, the Discovery Award in Proteomic Sciences from the [[Human Proteome Organization]] in 2013<ref>{{cite web|date=2 October 2013|title=Most important international proteomics award for Albert Heck|url=http://www.genomics.nl/News/2%20October%202013%20-%206.aspx|access-date=21 May 2014|publisher=Netherlands Genomics Initiative}}</ref> and the UePA Pioneer Proteomics Award in 2014.

Since 2014 he is a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]].<ref>{{cite web
| title = EMBO announces new members for 2013
| url = http://www.embo.org/news/press-releases/press-releases-2013/embo-announces-new-members-for-2013
| access-date = 21 May 2014
| publisher = EMBO
| date = 21 May 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| title = Albert Heck en Ineke Braakman verkozen tot EMBO leden
| url = http://www.uu.nl/faculty/science/NL/actueel/nieuwsfaculteit/Pages/Albert-Heck-en-Ineke-Braakman-verkozen-tot-EMBO-leden.aspx
| access-date = 21 May 2014
| publisher = Utrecht University
| date = 19 May 2014
| language = Dutch }}</ref> In 2014, Heck was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web
| title = KNAW kiest zeventien nieuwe leden
| url = https://www.knaw.nl/nl/actueel/nieuws/knaw-kiest-zeventien-nieuwe-leden
| access-date = 21 May 2014
| publisher = KNAW
| date = 21 May 2014
| language = Dutch }}</ref> The [[American Chemical Society]] honoured Albert Heck with the '[[Frank H. Field]] and [[Joe L. Franklin]] Award for Outstanding Achievements in Mass Spectrometry' in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|date=28 August 2015|title=Prestigious American Chemical Society awards for Albert Heck and Geert-Jan Boons|url=https://www.uu.nl/en/news/prestigious-american-chemical-society-awards-for-albert-heck-and-geert-jan-boons/|access-date=28 November 2019|publisher=UU}}</ref>

In 2017, he was awarded the [[Spinoza Prize]], the highest scientific distinction in the Netherlands for his "major contribution to the worldwide breakthrough of systematically mapping all proteins in human cells and their biological functions by means of mass spectrometry".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/news-and-events/news/2017/nwo-spinoza-prizes-awarded-to-eveline-crone-albert-heck-michel-orrit-and-alexander-van-oudenaarden.html|title=NWO Spinoza Prizes awarded to Eveline Crone, Albert Heck, Michel Orrit and Alexander van Oudenaarde|publisher=NWO|date=6 June 2017|access-date=28 November 2019}}</ref>

In 2018, he received the Sir Hans Krebs Medal of the [[Federation of European Biochemical Societies]] (FEBS) and the Thomson Medal Award of the [[International Mass Spectrometry Society]] (IMSC).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uu.nl/en/news/professor-albert-heck-is-to-receive-two-international-distinctions|title=Professor Albert Heck is to receive two international distinctions|publisher=UU|date=3 July 2018|access-date=28 November 2019}}</ref>
